title: Detection rate of GRPR-targeted PET in PSMA-negative prostate cancer in biochemical recurrence as a function of serum PSA and Gleason score
summary: Blood tests have shown that the prostate carcinoma has recurred; this situation is referred to as biochemical recurrence of prostate carcinoma. Targeted therapeutic approaches, such as external radiotherapy or surgery, often remain a curative option in your stage of the disease. However, reliable localisation of the cancerous tissue is of the utmost importance, as this could result in significant changes to the planned treatment strategy (e.g. change of plan for external radiotherapy). However, the PET/CT already performed on the prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) did not provide any evidence of the localisation of this tumour. It is therefore planned to carry out an additional PET/CT focussing on the gastrin-releasing hormone peptide receptor (GRPR). This GRPR is often found in high concentrations on the surface of prostate carcinoma cells. GRPR PET/CT therefore potentially enables precise localisation of the disease - even in cases where PSMA PET/CT is inconclusive.
conditions: OPS-Code 3-75:  Positron emission tomography with computed tomography [PET/CT]

interventions.name: one-time GRPR-directed PET in PSMA-negative prostate cancer

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
histologically confirmed prostate carcinoma after primary prostatectomy or radiotherapy, biochemical recurrence (PSA > 0.2 ng/ml after prostatectomy or increase in PSA more than 2.0 ng/ml above the nadir after definitive radiotherapy). All patients must have received a GRPR-directed PET as part of the clinical routine after a negative PSMA-PET/CT
Exclusion criteria:
Not available
